topicTitle: 3.4 Relative Atomic Mass and Atomic Mass Unit
stem: Briefly describe atomic mass, atomic number and atomic mass unit.
keyPoints: ["Mass number = protons + neutrons","Atomic number = protons","1 amu = 1/12 mass of C-12"]
modelAnswer: Atomic mass (nucleon or mass number) is the total number of protons and neutrons in an atom. Atomic number is the number of protons in its nucleus. One atomic mass unit is exactly one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.

stem: The isotope used to determine the path of carbon in photosynthesis is:
Determine the number of protons and neutrons in: (a) 12/6 C (b) 13/6 C (c) 14/6 C.
keyPoints: ["Protons = atomic number","Neutrons = mass number − atomic number","C-12: p6, n6; C-13: p6, n7; C-14: p6, n8"]
modelAnswer: For an isotope, protons equal the atomic number and neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number. Therefore: 12/6 C has 6 protons and 6 neutrons; 13/6 C has 6 protons and 7 neutrons; 14/6 C has 6 protons and 8 neutrons.

stem: What is meant by isotopes of an element? Give example of any element.
keyPoints: ["Same protons/atomic number","Different neutrons/mass number","Example: carbon isotopes"]
modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number (same number of protons) but different mass numbers because they contain different numbers of neutrons. Example: carbon-12, carbon-13 and carbon-14.

stem: Determine the number of protons and neutrons in 24/12 Mg, 25/12 Mg and 26/12 Mg.
keyPoints: ["Each Mg isotope: 12 protons","Mg-24: n12; Mg-25: n13; Mg-26: n14"]
modelAnswer: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so each isotope has 12 protons. Neutrons are mass number minus atomic number: 24/12 Mg has 12 neutrons, 25/12 Mg has 13 neutrons, and 26/12 Mg has 14 neutrons.

stem: What is meant by isotopes of an element? Give an example of any element.
keyPoints: ["Same atomic number/protons","Different neutrons","Example: Cl-35 and Cl-37"]
modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. For example, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 are isotopes of chlorine.

stem: Draw the structure of the following isotopes from their mass number and atomic number: H3, Cl36, Cl35 and U238.
